title: Regional fleet stress test worksheet for new LLM rollout
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet captures a focused stress test and capacity-impact analysis for the upcoming LLM v2 rollout (internal name: "Nova-70B-v2"). It is a working artifact to: 1) estimate KV cache memory footprint and GPU memory pressure per region under realistic traffic mixes, 2) define stress-test scenarios to exercise autoscaling and fallbacks, and 3) produce an actionable remediation plan (short + medium term) if capacity shortfalls appear.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Preliminary estimates show that Nova-70B-v2 increases per-session KV cache by ~2.6–3.8x versus our production baseline model family (approx. 45B decoders). With current regional A100/H100 pools and expected Q2 traffic growth, regions with <1200 effective GPU-80GB equivalents (us-west-2, eu-west-1) risk transient OOMs during peak synthetic sessions that hold long-lived chat contexts (>2k tokens). The stress-test below will validate whether our autoscaler + fallback policy keeps SLOs by 95th percentile latency under 600ms for streaming requests.

Assumptions (versioned):
- Model: Nova-70B-v2 (decoder-only), kv-per-token estimate: 36 bytes/token (conservative; includes key+value + indexing overhead + alignment); alternative low estimate: 24 bytes/token.
- Typical session: 3 contributors per user (2 user messages + 1 model response) => average context length at inference time: 1200 tokens.
- Percent of long-lived sessions (>=2k tokens): 12% during peak.
- GPU types: A100-80GB and H100-80GB, effective usable model memory per GPU for KV+model activations: 52 GB (model weights pinned) for A100; H100 similar but we conservatively use 52 GB.
- Average active concurrent sessions per GPU (baseline model): 18. Nova-70B-v2 reduces this by KV memory, new expected concurrent sessions per GPU: 6–12 depending on workload skew.
- Autoscaler adds GPU in batches of 4 per minute, max burst 32 GPUs per region.

Key calculations (worked examples):
1) KV footprint per session = kv_per_token * context_tokens. For conservative: 36 B/token * 1200 tokens = 43,200 B ~ 42.2 KB. Wait — check units: 36 bytes * 1200 = 43,200 bytes (~42 KB) – this is per head?
(IMPORTANT) We model per-layer & per-head duplication by multiplying by an architecture factor. For Nova-70B-v2 we observed an effective multiplier of 64 (layers*heads amortized factor) in memory accounting for KV storage style.
Therefore effective KV memory per session = 43,200 bytes * 64 = 2,764,800 B ~ 2.64 MB.

2) Sessions per GPU (KV-limited) = usable_GPU_memory / KV_per_session. Using usable 52 GB = 52 * 1024^3 bytes = 55,849,346,560 bytes. Sessions = 55,849,346,560 / 2,764,800 ≈ 20,200 sessions. This number is unrealistic because it assumes model activations and other allocations are zero. Instead we reserve 80% of usable GPU memory for model activations (quantized weights, KV indexing, workspace) and 20% for KV cache in shared scenarios. Effective KV pool for sessions = 0.20 * 55,849,346,560 ≈ 11,169,869,312 bytes => Sessions ≈ 4,040 concurrent sessions.

3) Realistic concurrency after accounting for activation+workspace: empirical adjustments from previous onboarding indicate a further 6x reduction when accounting for boked allocations, fragmentation, and runtime overhead (observed on similar 70B models). Adjusted sessions per GPU ≈ 4,040 / 6 ≈ 673 concurrent sessions (KV-limited).

4) Baseline concurrent sessions per GPU for production model family was 1,200 (after the same adjustments). So Nova-70B-v2 per-GPU concurrency represents ~56% of baseline, meaning we need roughly 1.8x GPU capacity to serve the same peak QPS if routing doesn't change.

Regional capacity snapshot (simplified table):
Region, GPUs (80GB equiv), Baseline concurrent sessions (estim.), New model concurrent sessions (calc), Shortfall multiplier
us-west-2, 950, 1,140, 636, 1.79
eu-west-1, 780, 936, 522, 1.79
us-east-1, 1,560, 1,872, 1,043, 1.80
asia-east1, 410, 492, 274, 1.80
(Note: table numbers assume baseline per-GPU concurrency = 1,200 and new per-GPU concurrency ≈ 673)

Scenario design (stress tests):
- Scenario A: Peak synthetic chat burst: 1-hour run, scaled 2x baseline QPS, 25% long-lived chats, no autoscaler. Goal: force KV cache pressure and observe OOM frequency and session rejection rates.
- Scenario B: Autoscaler latency exposure: same burst but with autoscaler on, burst policy min delay 2 min, max burst 32 GPUs. Goal: measure how often requests are queued > SLO and measure fallbacks to smaller models or cached responses.
- Scenario C: Regional outage cascade: simultaneously reduce region capacity by 40% for 20 min. Goal: verify cross-region routing and model-fallback correctness under KV eviction pressure.
- Scenario D: Cold-warm mix: 60% cold sessions (no prefix cache), 40% warm (prefix KVs cached on arrival). Goal: evaluate prefix-caching benefit and warmup latency.

Hypotheses to validate:
1) Autoscaler reactive policy will be insufficient to prevent SLO violations for bursts > 1.5x if long-lived sessions > 10% due to slow GPU add latency.
2) Prefix caching (per-cust pinned prefixes) can reduce effective KV per session by up to 45% for our prompt family and should be prioritized for heavy enterprise customers.
3) Eviction TTL of 10m leads to high re-warm rates under repeated short sessions; increasing to 30m dramatically reduces QPS-per-token costs but increases memory pressure.

Measured metrics to collect during runs:
- GPU memory used (kv_cache, activations) per GPU (time series, 1s resolution)
- OOMs and runtime-induced drops per minute
- 50/95/99 P99 latency for token generation and response start
- Queue length and average enqueue time
- Autoscaler events (scale-ups, scale-downs, time-to-provision)
- Cross-region reroute counts and fallbacks executed
- Cache hit ratio (prefix + kv) and effective KV bytes saved

Pass/fail criteria:
- Pass: P95 latency < 600ms for streaming start AND <0.5% request rejection due to memory OOMs during peak synthetic run with autoscaler enabled.
- Warning: P95 600–1200ms or 0.5–2% rejection rate.
- Fail: P95 > 1200ms or >2% rejection rate or >3 OOMs/min sustained.

Short-term mitigations (0–2 weeks):
- Route enterprise heavy contexts to Dedicated pools where customers can be pinned to capacity. Quick win: route customers flagged in rollout to dedicated on day-0. Owner: Solutions Eng (Ruth).
- Enable conservative per-session KV caps via runtime (limit max context tokens by default to 2,048; bump via quota). Owner: Serving-runtime (Michael).
- Increase KV eviction TTL from 10m -> 20m for warm prefixes only (A/B trial in us-west-2). Owner: Platform-Eng (Leo).

Medium-term (2–8 weeks):
- Evaluate kernel-level memory compaction improvements in runtime (PR#412 linked). Owner: Serving Runtime.
- Expand reserved GPU pool in high-pressure regions (us-west-2 + eu-west-1) by 40 GPUs each for Q2 (finance sign-off). Owner: Infra procurement.
- Implement cross-region spillover policy by model-family with prioritized fallback to compressed/quantized variant (Nova-70B-v2-q8).

Long-term (Q3+):
- Investigate model-splitting + KV sharding across host memory to allow higher session density per GPU.
- Improve autoscaler fast-path (reduce GPU add latency from ~60s to ~15s) via pre-warm ephemeral nodes.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Run Scenario A and D in us-west-2 test cluster (Asha, Michael) => ETA 2026-03-08
- Prepare routing flag to route rollout cohort to Dedicated by default (Ruth) => ETA 2026-03-12
- Finance approval request for +80 GPU supplemental pool (Infra procurement) => ETA 2026-03-20
- Instrument additional KV bytes metrics in telemetry pipeline (Leo) => ETA 2026-03-05

Open questions / unknowns to research:
- Exact Nova-70B-v2 internal kv_per_token multiplier; engineering has an internal microbenchmark but results vary by seq-len.
- Preemption behavior with current cloud provider for H100 reservations under cross-region spikes.
- Effectiveness of prefix-only caching for multi-turn assistant flows for top 10 enterprise customers (we need customer prompt sets).

Notes / References:
- See linked PR and confluence doc IDs above. Use test cluster tag: infra-rollout-nova-v2.
- Keep this doc living; update after each scenario run with measured numbers (replace conservative estimates).

Appendix: quick calculation cheat sheet
- KV bytes = kv_per_token * tokens * arch_multiplier
- Effective sessions per GPU (eme) = floor((usable_gpu_bytes * kv_allocation_fraction) / KV_bytes) / runtime_overhead_factor
- Required GPUs = ceil(expected_peak_sessions / eme)

End of worksheet.
